## What Is a TransDigm Group Internship?


A TransDigm internship or co-op is a placement at one of 50+ independently managed operating units, each designing and manufacturing proprietary aerospace components. Unlike centralized programs at Boeing or Lockheed Martin, TransDigm's decentralized model means Arkwin Industries, Korry Electronics, Data Device Corporation, and Calspan each run their own hiring. The corporate level offers a **Management Development Program** for MBA graduates and a **Junior Military Officer Program** , but undergraduate positions exist only at the operating-unit level. This means small teams (100-500 employees), direct exposure to flight-critical hardware, and rapid responsibility escalation. TransDigm promotes from within:[two-thirds or more of senior leadership positions are filled internally](https://www.transdigm.com/community-impact/talent-development/) .

Each of 50+ operating units posts and fills positions independently, with some offering year-round co-ops (Arkwin has confirmed Spring and Fall 2027 co-ops). The best strategy is to identify 3-5 operating units aligned with your engineering discipline and monitor their postings on Indeed and LinkedIn. The corporate Management Development Program (MBA only) follows structured fall recruiting.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Eligibility varies by operating unit, but aerospace/defense industry norms apply:


• **Education:** currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student in engineering (mechanical, aerospace, electrical, systems engineering).


• **Work authorization:** US citizenship often required due to ITAR regulations and defense contract classifications. Some commercial aviation units may accept permanent residents.


• **GPA:** not specified at the corporate level; varies by operating unit.


• **Security clearance:** some positions at defense-focused subsidiaries may require or initiate security clearance processes.


### Why Does TransDigm Require US Citizenship for Many Positions?


TransDigm manufactures components classified under International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Employees who access controlled technical data must be US persons (citizens or permanent residents). This applies to most engineering co-ops at defense-focused units. Commercial aviation subsidiaries may have more flexibility. Check each posting individually.

Mechanical design, CAD proficiency, and materials knowledge are foundational. Electrical engineering matters for avionics and power systems units. The differentiator is sole-source aerospace expertise: understanding how proprietary components are designed, qualified, and maintained for aircraft with decades-long lifecycles.

## What Is the TransDigm Group Application and Interview Process Like?


TransDigm's hiring varies by operating unit. The general pattern for engineering co-ops:


1. **Identify target operating units.** Research which of TransDigm's 50+ subsidiaries aligns with your engineering discipline. Search subsidiary names on Indeed and LinkedIn.


2. **Apply directly to the subsidiary.** No centralized portal exists. Submit through the subsidiary's career page or via Indeed/LinkedIn.


3. **Phone screen with subsidiary HR.** Background, engineering interests, and availability. Expect questions about why aerospace components.


4. **Technical interview with engineering team.** Role-specific questions about design, materials, or electrical systems. Some units include a facility tour.


5. **Background check and offer.** Many positions require US citizenship verification. Security clearance processes may add time.


Know which subsidiary you are targeting and what it makes. TransDigm's 50+ units span hydraulic actuators to cockpit displays to flight test operations. ## How Do You Stand Out at the Hidden Giant of Aerospace?


Three moves, all executable before fall 2026. First, identify the specific subsidiary and learn its product line. Arkwin makes hydraulic actuators. Korry makes cockpit displays. Data Device makes MIL-STD data bus products. In your interview, demonstrate you know what the subsidiary builds and why that niche interests you. Second, understand the sole-source model. TransDigm's components are often the only option for an aircraft platform, meaning the engineering work is critical and products have decades-long lifecycles. Frame your interest around reliability and precision. Third, prepare for the citizenship question proactively. If you are a US citizen, state it clearly. If you are a permanent resident, check the specific posting. International students should focus on commercial aviation units with more flexibility.

## FAQ


### Does TransDigm have a centralized internship program?


No. TransDigm operates a highly decentralized model where each of its 50-plus operating units manages its own hiring. There is no single career portal for undergraduate internships. The corporate level offers a Management Development Program for MBA graduates only.


### How do I find TransDigm internships?


Search individual subsidiary names on Indeed and LinkedIn: Arkwin Industries, Korry Electronics, Data Device Corporation, Calspan, CMC Electronics, Champion Aerospace. Each unit posts co-ops and internships through its own channels.


### Does TransDigm require US citizenship for interns?


Many positions require US citizenship due to ITAR regulations and defense classifications. Commercial aviation subsidiaries may have more flexibility. Check each posting individually and state your citizenship status clearly in your application.


### What is the TransDigm Management Development Program?


The MDP is for recent MBA graduates: three 8-month rotations at different operating units, transitioning to permanent management. This is NOT an undergraduate internship. TransDigm University, a partnership with USC Marshall, is for current employees only.


### How much do TransDigm interns get paid?


Specific data is limited due to the decentralized structure. Aerospace engineering co-ops typically pay $20 to $30 per hour. TransDigm's 47% operating margins and strong financials suggest competitive compensation within the aerospace components sector.


### Where are TransDigm operating units located?


Across the US and internationally: Cleveland OH (HQ), Westbury NY (Arkwin), Everett WA (Korry), Bohemia NY (Data Device), Buffalo NY (Calspan), Liberty SC (Champion), Montreal (CMC Electronics), and many more.


### What engineering disciplines does TransDigm hire?


Mechanical, aerospace, electrical, and systems engineering are most common. Some units hire for materials science, quality engineering, and manufacturing engineering. The specific discipline depends on which subsidiary you target.


### Can a TransDigm co-op lead to a full-time job?


Yes. TransDigm promotes two-thirds or more of senior leadership from within, indicating strong internal career pathways. Full-time offers come from the specific operating unit where you interned. The decentralized model means your relationship is with the subsidiary, not corporate.
